texts.preamble: Ashoksinh Vikramsinh Rajput vs State Of Gujarat & 5 on 4 December, 2015 Bench: Jayant Patel, Vipul M. Pancholi C/Sca/9925/2015 Order
texts.facts: The petitioner initially preferred the petition, which was heard by the learned Single Judge, but thereafter, the learned Single Judge found that the petition involves larger public interest and, therefore, the matter was referred to the HC-NIC Page 1 of 6 The petition thereafter is treated as Public Interest Litigation (PIL). The petitioner, for espousing the cause mentioned in the petition, is seeking appropriate directions against the respondents to initiate proceedings under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') against the manufacturer of AAVA Natural Mineral Water, contending, inter alia, that the advertisement is misleading and there is misbranding of the product and the prayer is made that such would be in the larger public interest. 3. In response to the notice issued by this Court, affidavits-in-reply have been filed by the respondents.
texts.arguments: Upon hearing the learned Counsel for both the sides, it appears to us that the contention of the petitioner is that the product is misbranded and it is not natural mineral water, which is being sold by respondent No.6, whereas, as per respondent No.6, there is no misbranding of the product and the product, which is being sold, is natural mineral water. 6. As per the petitioner, the samples were taken, but it did not meet with the standards, whereas, as per respondent No.6 as well as Food Analyst, who is represented by the AGP and respondent No.5 - Bureau of Indian Standards, it meets with the requirements. There are allegations and counter- allegations, but considering the facts and circumstances, we find that if the testing of the water, which is being marketed and sold by respondent No.6, is undertaken by competent authority under Section 47 of the Act, such would not cause any prejudice, since even otherwise also, as per the mechanism of the Act, Food Analyst or the competent authority under the Act HC-NIC Page 3 of 6 Created On Thu Dec 10 00:27:35 IST 2015 has power to take the samples and undertake the testing. 7. The essential attempt on the part of the petitioner was to see that the authority is activated for appropriate action in accordance with law. 9. Even Mr.Kavina, learned Sr. Counsel for respondent No.6, has not opposed the same, contending that the product, which is being marketed by them, is meeting with the requirements and there could not be any objection for undertaking the test.
